svg.title: Evolution — phases concept R4: the paramecium and the stentor, dead ends with three options
svg.desc: Ciliates never became many-celled. Option A keeps them as the last great single cells with real upgrades (trichocysts, conjugation, anchored crowds, regrowth); B borrows a colonial ciliate; C switches road. Code-drawn.
svg.text: EVOLUTION
· concept R4 — THE CILIATES · the paramecium and the stentor stay one cell
In real life neither line ever became many-celled: they bet on one huge, complicated cell. Three ways to handle that in the game.
ticket #782 · epic #761
dark-field language of sheets 01 and 04 · zero raster
A · STAY ONE CELL: the last great single cells (recommended)
real upgrades from their own biology; they become the pond's specialists
Trichocysts: fires a burst of tiny harpoons

text.font-family: JetBrains Mono, DejaVu Sans Mono, Consolas, Menlo, monospace

svg.text: a real defence against Didinium · a new active ability
Conjugation: pair up and swap one trait

text.font-family: JetBrains Mono, DejaVu Sans Mono, Consolas, Menlo, monospace

svg.text: real sex in a single cell · co-op without a merged body
The anchored crowd: stentors that share a current

text.font-family: JetBrains Mono, DejaVu Sans Mono, Consolas, Menlo, monospace

svg.text: anchor, and nearby stentors pool their whirlpools: food from farther
Regrowth: a bitten stentor regrows from a piece

text.font-family: JetBrains Mono, DejaVu Sans Mono, Consolas, Menlo, monospace

svg.text: a real feat · the ciliate answer to the colony's spare lives
Also for both:
• the tier-II and tier-III form
upgrades that no round reaches
today get a home in the pond
• the pond's specialists: fast
hunters of small colonies
B · A BORROWED COLONY ROAD
the stentor grows a branching tree of bell-cells on one shared stalk
Real model: Zoothamnium,
a colonial bell ciliate.
But it is a different
family from the stentor,
and the paramecium has
no real road at all:
we would invent one.
C · SWITCH ROAD WHEN COLONIES ARRIVE
at 17:00 a ciliate player picks one of the three real roads
green road
gathering road
glass road
Simple to build;
but you drop the
form you chose.
D · THE REAL STORY, AND WHY A
these are the forms that elongate: the paramecium slipper and the stentor trumpet (the euglena has the green road)
True
Ciliates (paramecium, stentor) never evolved a many-celled body. Instead each is one of the most complex cells alive, with two kinds of nucleus.
Paramecium fires trichocysts, tiny harpoons, when Didinium attacks; it reproduces by splitting and has sex by conjugation, swapping nuclei with a partner.
Stentor coeruleus (up to ~2 mm) can regrow a whole cell from a small piece (Tartar, "The Biology of Stentor", 1961), and anchored stentors that settle close together
feed better by pooling their currents (Shekhar et al., Current Biology 2023).
The paramecium even shaped multicellular life: a green alga hunted by paramecia evolved clusters in the lab (Herron et al., Scientific Reports 2019).
Recommendation: A
It is true to life, it teaches something ("not every line goes multicellular"), and it keeps the form the player chose. B invents biology; C throws the choice away.
The cost: the ciliates need their own pond upgrades (about 3 tickets), and the pond needs to make one big fast cell as viable as a colony (a balance job).
